channel.title: Case Study Room: Newborn Health in Liberia
channel.description: Study audio for a global health case competition: history, today's health system, why newborns die, the core question, ways to think about solutions, and competition day.
channel.itunes:author: Case Study Room

item.title: 0. Quick start
item.description: The five things to understand before the competition: the size of the gap, when and why newborns die, the three delays, why progress stalled, and how the day works.

item.title: 1. Geography and history
item.description: Rainforest, coast and six months of rain; from Indigenous peoples and the American Colonization Society to civil war, the women's peace movement, Ebola and today. How each chapter shaped newborn health.

item.title: 2. The health system today
item.description: Facilities, staff, who pays, donor dependence, the 2025 U.S. aid cuts, and the community health workers and Trained Traditional Midwives who reach remote homes.

item.title: 3. Why newborns die
item.description: The first week and first day; prematurity, asphyxia and infection; the three delays; and the deeper causes: poverty, schooling, gender, violence, geography.

item.title: 4. The core question
item.description: Liberia's newborn deaths fell fast until 2010, then stalled, while neighbours kept improving and facility births doubled. Two hosts debate what the real problem is.

item.title: 5. Thinking about solutions
item.description: Tools for building your own idea: PIH's 5 S's, the logic model, scoring ideas, families of approaches, common traps, and a made-up practice case.

item.title: 6. Critique of a worked example
item.description: A friendly but honest critique of one example pitch, 'First Day, Every Baby': what works, what's missing, and how a team could improve or replace it.

item.title: 7. Competition day
item.description: Reading the prompt, the team timeline, building a story, slides, rehearsal, judges' questions, and what to do when things go wrong.
